title: Edge-case hardware profile bundle publisher and pin revalidation for mixed-batch workloads
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Goal: Build a profile bundle publisher and automated pin revalidation workflow that handles hardware-specific edge cases we observe when onboarding large models across A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants, especially under mixed-batch and microburst traffic patterns.

Background and motivation:
- Current onboarding publishes single 'stable' performance signatures that assume steady-state batching. We've seen customer regressions when prefix-cache usage, short sequence bursts, or mixed per-request batch sizes change latency envelopes on certain SKUs (notably MI300 under 4k quantized tokens and H100 under mixed fp16/4-bit quantization).
- Pinning currently expires only on manual re-pin or major model version changes. We need automated revalidation so that pins degrade safely when telemetry indicates drift.

Scope and deliverables:
1) "profile-bundle" format: canonical JSON artifact that bundles per-SKU latency P50/P90/P99, cold/warm startup deltas, quantization sensitivity notes, and a minimal compatibility shim listing which runtime kernels and flags were used. Bundle must include an immutable signature and a semantic version.
2) Publisher service: CLI + API to publish bundles to the model catalog with per-region SKU mapping and optional public/unlisted visibility. Publisher must validate size (<128KB), schema version, and run a quick synthetic microbenchmark on a pinned canary pool for sanity checks.
3) Pin revalidation policy: a scheduled probe (daily) that compares live telemetry to published bundle envelopes. If P99 exceeds published P99 by configurable margin or cold-start regressions exceed threshold, create automated rollout to fallback variant and open alert/issue.
4) Compatibility table: algorithm to determine whether a bundle is usable as-is on a runtime variant (eg. MI300-64GB with certain kernel kludges).

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Frequency of republishing vs stability: frequent republishes reduce exposure to drift but increase churn for downstream customers. Decision: make republish lightweight but require explicit major semantic version bump for changes in compatibility guarantees.
- Size vs fidelity of signatures: storing full microbenchmark histograms is expensive. Decision: keep histograms in archival store and publish compact percentiles and a histogram hash in the bundle.
- Automated pin revalidation aggressiveness: tuning required to avoid noisy rollbacks. Start conservative (10% margin on P99, 24-hours sustained) and allow PM/SE to opt-in to tighter SLAs.

Acceptance criteria (summary below in separate field) and implementation checklist are included.
acceptance_criteria: A profile-bundle JSON conforms to the new schema v1 and can be consumed by the catalog API without schema errors.
Publisher runs synthetic sanity checks against a small canary pool for all four SKUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) and returns pass/fail with logs.
Automated revalidation job runs daily; when telemetry continuously exceeds thresholds for 24 hours, it creates a manifested fallback rollout and opens an ENG ticket.
Bundles published to the catalog are searchable by model, semantic version, SKU, and region; bundle size enforcement is active (<128KB).
Compatibility table algorithm flags at least 90% of known model/variant combinations correctly in testing harness (unit tests and synthetic regression suite).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Evelyn Chen: Initial ticket created after customer incident where a quantized LLM on MI300 saw 35% P99 regression during mixed-batch bursts. Attached incident notes and telemetry snapshot.

2025-02-20 - Marco Duarte: Spike completed. Confirmed that H100 FP16 path and MI300 4-bit quantized path diverge on KV cache warmup behavior. Proposal: add 'cold_warm_delta' field to bundle and require publishing synthetic 3-minute burst test. (see confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Hardware+Profile+Bundle+Design)

2025-02-25 - Aisha Patel (PM): Reviewed trade-offs. PM asks that republish on minor semantic changes should be opt-in for Dedicated customers. Also requested UI visibility in console for bundle semantic history.

2025-02-27 - PR feedback (ENG): Draft implementation PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872. Highlights: new schema, publisher CLI, quick-microbench harness. Requested to split publisher and revalidation into separate commits for easier rollback.

2025-03-02 - Marco Duarte: Integration test failures on CI for L40S due to different kernel selection. Added a runtime shim to map kernel flags; will add unit test. Patch pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4901

2025-03-04 - Reliability team (notes): Determined SLO for pin revalidation should be 99.9% for hosted API. Added requirement to surface revalidation events to SLO dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/slo/pins
notes: Implementation approach: two-phase rollout. Phase 1: publish bundles as 'candidate' and use only for internal routing. Phase 2: allow customers to opt into 'auto-pin' behavior in console.
We should add a small TTL and monotonic version check so that older bundles never silently overwrite newer ones in the catalog. Semantic versions are mandatory for compatibility guarantees.
Ops runbook: If automated revalidation triggers a rollback, notify owner + create incident with the last-good bundle ID and the telemetry diff hash.
